extracted.intended_audience: school districts, postsecondary institutions, State athletic associations, athletic administrators, Title IX coordinators, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts standards from the Department of Education's proposed Title IX regulation governing use of sex-related athletic eligibility criteria that would limit or deny students' opportunity to participate on male or female teams consistent with their gender identity. Focuses on legal tests, scope, permissible objectives, and required safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria covered by the proposed regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation governs only sex-related criteria that would limit or deny a student's eligibility to participate on a male or female team consistent with their gender identity; criteria unrelated to sex (e.g., attendance or GPA requirements) are outside its scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of covered criteria include requirements tied to how a student's sex is determined for team-eligibility purposes (such as sex markers on identification documents) and requirements for physical examinations, medical testing, or treatment related to a student's sex characteristics if those results could be used to limit or deny participation consistent with gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'limit' and 'deny' eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Limit' eligibility means not allowing transgender students to participate fully on a team consistent with their gender identity (e.g., permitting participation in some but not all competitions). 'Deny' eligibility means foreclosing the opportunity to participate on male or female teams consistent with gender identity (e.g., requiring participation consistent with sex assigned at birth or prohibiting transgender girls who underwent endogenous puberty from girls' teams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulation applies only where the criteria either limit or deny participation as defined above; criteria that merely regulate non-sex aspects of participation fall outside the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially related to achievement of an important educational objective
rubrics_metrics.description: If sex-related criteria would limit or deny participation consistent with gender identity, they must, for each sport, level of competition, and grade or education level, be substantially related to achieving an important educational objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substantial-relationship standard requires a direct, substantial relationship between the objective and the means used (analogous to standards in 34 CFR 106.34 and Equal Protection case law). Criteria relying on overbroad generalizations about male/female talents, capacities, or preferences will not satisfy the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important educational objectives (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation does not limit which objectives may be asserted, but examples of possible important educational objectives include ensuring fairness in competition and prevention of sports-related injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may assert such objectives, particularly for older students or highly competitive programs, but must demonstrate that the criteria genuinely serve the asserted objective for the specific sport/level/grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited or impermissible asserted objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not satisfy the rule by asserting objectives that communicate or codify disapproval of a student's gender identity, that are solely aimed at excluding transgender students from sports, that require adherence to sex stereotypes, or that exist only for administrative convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives that are pretextual, punitive, or rooted in moral disapproval are inadequate (citing cases like Hecox, Romer v. Evans, Virginia). The justification must be genuine, not invented post hoc in response to litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize harms to affected students
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex-related criteria that would limit or deny participation must minimize harms to students whose opportunity to participate consistent with their gender identity would be limited or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes specific harms from exclusion (e.g., exacerbation of gender dysphoria, stigma, outing, invasion of privacy, denial of educational and social benefits). Recipients must account for and attempt to minimize these harms when designing or applying criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sport-, level-, and grade-specific assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria must be applied and justified on a sport-by-sport, level-of-competition, and grade-or-education-level basis rather than via a one-size-fits-all rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation requires assessment of whether the criterion is substantially related to the objective in the specific context (nature of each sport, level of competition, grade), and categorical exclusions across all sports/levels will generally fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based and individualized analysis (no overbroad generalizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria must be supported by evidence showing a direct relationship to fairness or safety concerns in the particular sport/level, and cannot rest on broad assumptions that all transgender individuals have unfair physical advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites IOC guidance encouraging evidence-based restrictions and court rulings rejecting proxy assumptions (e.g., that transgender status is a legitimate proxy for performance). Recipients should use sport-specific evidence rather than categorical assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of sex-related eligibility criteria (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of sex-related criteria that could fall within the regulation's scope include reliance on sex markers on identification documents (birth certificate, passport, driver's license) and requirements for physical examinations, medical testing, or medical treatment (e.g., testosterone suppression) that could be used to limit or deny eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such criteria, when they would limit or deny participation, must meet the substantial-relationship and minimize-harm requirements; the proposed rule does not categorically ban these mechanisms but requires justification and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing §106.41(b) discretion preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed regulation does not affect a recipient's existing discretion under current §106.41(b) to offer separate male and female athletic teams where selection is based on competitive skill or the activity is a contact sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain the ability to have sex-separated teams under existing regulations in those specific circumstances, but any sex-related criteria that limit/deny participation must still comply with the proposed regulation's requirements when they implicate gender-identity participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives and mitigation strategies to eligibility restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools and associations may pursue alternatives to sex-based eligibility exclusions—such as coaching/training, protective equipment, rule modifications, and generally applicable competition rules—to address fairness or safety concerns without denying participation consistent with gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder feedback cited in the preamble indicates these strategies can often achieve fairness and injury-prevention goals, especially at pre-collegiate and non-elite levels; recipients should consider such measures before adopting restrictive sex-related eligibility criteria.
